abstract:
Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is closely linked to chronic inflammation, but the transcriptional mechanisms connecting epithelial inflammatory remodeling with malignant transformation remain incompletely understood.
We integrated secondary analysis of published single-cell epithelial transition-state data, virtual SP1 perturbation, TCGA analyses, xCell immune infiltration analysis, TIDE-based exploratory immunotherapy prediction, Co-IP/MS, and a 4NQO-induced mouse model to investigate SP1-associated network remodeling during ESCC carcinogenesis.
SP1 regulatory importance increased across pairwise epithelial state comparisons. In adjacent normal epithelial cells, virtual SP1 overexpression affected genes linked to inflammatory response, NF-κB-related signaling, epithelial stress remodeling, and proliferation. SP1 expression correlated with immune infiltration features and immune checkpoint gene expression, and TIDE analysis suggested an association with predicted immunotherapy-related features. SP1-binding partners were enriched in RNA metabolism, RNA splicing, and nuclear protein-complex annotations, suggesting potential non-canonical regulatory associations that require further experimental validation.
SP1 may represent a progressively enhanced transcriptional hub during inflammation-associated ESCC carcinogenesis, with state-dependent network remodeling spanning epithelial inflammatory stress, malignant transformation, and tumor immune features.
